newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel vows to go ahead with Bezeq telecom sale.
newsitem.headline: Israel vows to go ahead with Bezeq telecom sale.

text.p: Israel vowed on Friday to sell off more of Bezeq Israel Telecom after persuading 60,000 state workers to end a one-day protest strike over the company's privatisation.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said the sides had agreed at a late-night meeting to try to iron out their disagreements within a week.
The nationwide strike in solidarity with Bezeq workers had grounded travellers at Tel Aviv's international airport and disrupted rail and postal services.

"The prime minister further announced the government intends to carry out the Bezeq company share offering of up to 52 percent as soon as possible and on the basis of the financial reports of June 1997," a statement said.

"It was agreed during the meeting that within a period of time not to exceed two months the sides will agree on an alternative if necessary in the event the share offering is not carried out," it said.
"The prime minister further announced any further dilution of the company's holdings up to 52 percent will be done only after fulfilment of the above."
The statement said that based on these understandings, the workers had agreed to return to work.

State workers declared the stoppage on Wednesday hours after the government issued an order to force hundreds of Bezeq employees to restore essential telephone services disrupted in their week-long strike at the country's main telecoms provider.
Union leaders at Bezeq had protested at government plans to privatise more of the state-owned company through the $250 million sale of 12.5 percent of its stock to Merrill Lynch.

The union leaders insisted the Merrill Lynch deal violated government promises to involve Bezeq workers in all aspects of the company's privatisation and called for the sale to be cancelled or to use its revenues to fund early pension plans.
The government has already floated 24 percent of Bezeq but in 1995 Britain's Cable and Wireless PLC bought up about 10 percent of the public float on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.
